neighbours.label: the subword 'om'/'rom' inside telomere/centromere terms (tel|om|ere, cent|rom|ere)
fire: Each time a cell divides, its telomeres become slightly shorter.
Cancer cells often reactivate telomerase to keep dividing indefinitely.
The researchers measured telomere length in blood samples from twins.
Spindle fibres attach to the centromere during cell division.
In this species the centromeres sit close to one end of each chromosome.
Short telomeres have been linked to faster biological ageing.
The enzyme telomerase adds repeats to the ends of chromosomes.
We stained the centromeric regions with a fluorescent probe.
quiet: Each time a cell divides, its chromosomes must be copied exactly.
Cancer cells often switch off tumour suppressors to keep dividing indefinitely.
The researchers measured chromatin density in blood samples from twins.
Spindle fibres attach to the kinetochore during cell division.
In this species the genes sit close to one end of each chromosome.
Damaged DNA has been linked to faster biological ageing.
The enzyme polymerase adds nucleotides to the growing strand.
We stained the nuclear envelope with a fluorescent probe.

notes: Card top examples are tel⟦om⟧eres, cent⟦rom⟧eres, tel⟦om⟧erase; tokenizer check: ' telomeres' -> tel|om|eres. Near misses keep chromosome biology without these words.
